text:
maya: quick heads-up — our telemetry shows ~8% of requests dropping the project claim after the recent routing-fallback change. that chunk is being billed to org-level quota and tripping org ratebands :grimacing:

sam: ouch. do we know which path loses it? proxy vs direct routing?

maya: looks like requests that hit the edge proxy and get routed to fallback model (compat-mode) sometimes come back with only `org_id` in the signed header. example header we see: `X-Redwood-Origin: org/123` (no project segment)

alex: can you paste a sanitized header dump? curious if it's a signing bug or upstream rewrite.

maya: pasted a small sample below (sanitized):

```
X-Redwood-Origin: org/123
X-Redwood-Service: svc-llm-router
X-Redwood-Signature: sig_***
```

no `project/` piece.

priya: are these coming from ephemeral service accounts or customer API keys? different fallout either way.

maya: mostly customer API keys (project-scoped). ephemerals are fine.

sam: timeline — this started after we flipped the fallback routing to prefer cheaper variant when capacity low?

maya: yep, flip deployed last wednesday. rollout was 30% -> 100% over 24h. spike matched that window.

jen: UX/console angle — product teams will see org-level quota burn without obvious request attribution. we should show "routing-decisions" in the per-request trace in the console (small flag) so users can see when a fallback variant was used and which claim was present.

alex: implementation-wise we have two hypotheses: 1) the fallback path intentionally strips project claims when exchanging tokens to a compatible model (legacy shim), 2) header signing truncation in the edge when we rewrite for compatibility.

sam: what does the auth-service do when it gets a request lacking project claim? fallback to org-only and mint a short-lived exchange token for the model pool. that sounds like hypothesis 1.

maya: agree. logs show auth-service issuing exchange tokens without project claim for ~75% of these.

priya: then the fix surface is auth-service. but we need to be careful: some models don't accept project-bound tokens and the shim historically stripped claims to make them work. we can't break older tenants.

jen: proposal: add a telemetry label `routing.exchange.project_present:true|false` and surface a console heatmap for the next week. also add a small console banner for affected orgs explaining increased org quota usage and how to opt-in to strict-project-routing.

alex: +1 for telemetry label. also add `routing.reason` enumerated (`capacity`, `compat-mode`, `region-fallback`) so we can pivot.

sam: rollout plan: 1) turn on exchange.project_present telemetry at 10% (hot path) 2) enable a canary config that forces auth-service to preserve project claim whenever possible (opt-in for a few internal orgs) 3) measure false-negatives where model rejects project-bound tokens 4) fallback to original stripping behavior if rejection > 1%

maya: i've kicked off a dashboard ticket: infra#842 to track the heatmap + `routing.reason` breakdown. i've attached a quick query snippet for telemetry team:

```
SELECT
  routing_reason, exchange_project_present, count(*) as requests,
  sum(case when status='quota_denied' then 1 else 0 end) as quota_denials
FROM telemetry.requests
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days' AND channel = 'api'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY requests DESC;
```

sam: can we also log `original_header` for a short retention window (PII scrubbed) to help debug?

priya: okay for internal orgs, but we should not retain customer headers long-term. scrub and ttl 48h. legal signed off on that pattern last quarter.

jen: UX note — console action: add an "Investigate routing" link next to quota spikes that opens the heatmap and example traces. short-term we can add a tooltip explaining what "routing.exchange.project_present=false" means.

maya: deploy-bot: starting canary config to preserve project claims for internal-tenants flag `auth.preserve_project_claim=true` on prod-canary.

deploy-bot: canary started for 3 internal orgs at 1777771400 — monitor `routing.exchange_project_present` and `model_reject_rate` on dashboards.

alex: I'll watch model rejection metric. if rejection spike, i'll post rollback checklist.

sam: great. next steps: maya to validate telemetry label coverage, alex to monitor rejections, jen to wire the console tooltip + quick link, priya to confirm header retention TTL. follow-up in 24h and decision to roll to customers after 72h. :eyes:

maya: thanks all — will update in thread with first heatmap snapshot.
